intent: Cover artificial turf projects for Commerce City, CO and the folded-in unincorporated community of Derby: soil and drainage, HOA/state turf law, water provider and current drought-stage watering rules, and sports-field turf availability under state law.
distinctValue: Vona sandy loam ground with 0-1% slope drives compaction/drainage planning rather than clay; SB23-178 protects backyard turf from HOA bans while HOAs still control front yards; HB25-1113 exempts sports fields/playgrounds from the new ban on nonfunctional turf; South Adams County Water and Sanitation District serves both Commerce City and Derby and is currently under Stage 1 drought restrictions; Derby itself is unincorporated Adams County, not Commerce City, so city permits/ordinances don't reach it.

sources.label: USDA Soil Data Access (SSURGO)
supports: Vona sandy loam: about 66.6% sand and 10% clay, well drained, on slopes of 0 to 1%

sources.label: Commerce City, Colorado (Wikipedia)
supports: most homes built since 2000 in the Northern Range north of I-76

sources.label: Colorado SB23-178, signed act
supports: HOA design guidelines can't prohibit nonvegetative turf behind a detached home

sources.label: Buffalo Run Golf Course
supports: 18-hole, par-72 course designed by Keith Foster, with six sets of tees

sources.label: DICK'S Sporting Goods Park
supports: Colorado Rapids' stadium with a Fields Complex that can be rented

sources.label: Colorado HB25-1113, signed act
supports: bars local governments from letting nonfunctional artificial turf into new commercial, institutional or HOA common-area landscaping; functional artificial turf includes sports fields and playgrounds

sources.label: City of Commerce City: water service
supports: water service is provided by South Adams County Water and Sanitation District, not the city

sources.label: Derby, Colorado (Wikipedia)
supports: an unincorporated community and a census-designated place (CDP) located in and governed by Adams County, Colorado

sources.label: South Adams County Water and Sanitation District: conservation
supports: Stage 1 Drought currently in effect, declared Wednesday, May 13, 2026
2 days/week outdoor watering based on your address
20% surcharge applies to usage above the first tier, for every thousand gallons above 11,999 gallons per month
installing new sod is strongly discouraged during June-August; new sod may only be installed during April, May, September, or October under Stage 1 restrictions
new sod and seed may be watered for no more than 21 consecutive days, after which watering is limited to twice weekly based on the mandatory irrigation schedule
